## Load packages

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, limpa, limma, tibble, writexl)
here::i_am("01_Preprocess/02_Quantification/a_script/02_quantify.qmd")
```

## Read measurements and protein estimates

`y` holds the filtered precursors from `01_Filtering`. `proteins` holds the protein estimates and
their standard errors that `02_quantify_run.R` saved, because `dpcQuant()` takes about 100 minutes
and this notebook should render in minutes. The checkpoint must have used every filtered
precursor; if filtering changes, rerun the script.

```{r read}
y <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "01_Filtering", "c_data", "precursors_filtered.rds"))

checkpoints <- here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "quant_runs")
sensitivity_file <- file.path(checkpoints, "proteins_slope_fitted.rds")
proteins <- readRDS(file.path(checkpoints, "proteins_slope_0.7.rds"))
stopifnot(sum(proteins$genes$NPrec) == nrow(y))

dim(y)
dim(proteins)
head(proteins$genes, 6)
```

## Missingness

In DIA data, low-intensity precursors go missing more often. The plot takes the precursor matrix
and shows the proportion of missing values against mean observed intensity; a downward trend is
that association.

```{r ave-vs-mis}
plotAveVsMis(y)
```

## Fit the detection curve

The detection probability curve (DPC) gives the probability that a precursor is observed as a
function of its true intensity, through an intercept and a slope. `dpc()` takes the log2 matrix and
returns the fitted pair. Its default, `model = "cn"`, is `dpcCN()`, the complete-normal estimator
the limpa FAQ recommends for noisy data, fitted on a stratified subset of 2,000 precursors.

```{r dpc}
dpcest <- dpc(y$E)
plotDPC(dpcest)

dpc_parameters <- tibble(intercept = dpcest$dpc[1], slope = dpcest$dpc[2])
round(dpc_parameters, 3)
```

The fitted slope, `r round(dpcest$dpc[2], 3)`, sits below the 0.7 to 0.9 band the limpa FAQ calls
typical for DIA-NN with match-between-runs. The FAQ's advice for that case is the project's choice
for the primary run: "If `dpcCN()` doesn't give a value in that range, it would be reasonable to
run `dpcQuant()` with a preset value `dpc.slope=0.7`." Standard errors or hit counts alone do not
show which slope is right, so the fitted slope is kept as a sensitivity run (below and in
`02_Differential`).

## Roll-up

`02_quantify_run.R` combines precursors into proteins with `dpcQuant()`, grouping by
`Protein.Group`. It returns a complete matrix, an abundance for every protein in every sample,
plus a standard error per value; `dpcDE()` later uses those to predict each protein's variance.
The loaded checkpoint holds `r format(nrow(proteins), big.mark = ",")` protein groups from
`r format(nrow(y), big.mark = ",")` precursors. The curve it used, slope preset and intercept
estimated by limpa:

```{r used-curve}
round(proteins$dpc, 3)
```

## Detection filter

`filterByDetection()` takes the protein object and a minimum number of samples, and returns one
`TRUE` or `FALSE` per protein. Its help page leaves the threshold to the analyst for a large
dataset; here it is the smallest group size. The count runs across all samples, so it does not
guarantee detection within any one group.

```{r detection}
group_sizes <- table(proteins$targets$group)
detected <- filterByDetection(proteins, n.samples = min(group_sizes))
proteins <- proteins[detected, ]

group_sizes
c(before = length(detected), kept = sum(detected), dropped = sum(!detected))
```

## Normalisation

Cyclic loess (`normalizeBetweenArrays(method = "cyclicloess")`) removes abundance-dependent
differences between samples. DIA-NN normalised the precursors already; this second pass works on
the protein estimates. Smyth recommends quantile or cyclic loess normalisation of limpa protein
quantifications when sample differences are technical
([Bioconductor support](https://support.bioconductor.org/p/9163187/#9163221)).

```{r normalise}
unnormalised <- proteins$E
proteins$E <- normalizeBetweenArrays(proteins$E, method = "cyclicloess")
```

Intensity distributions before and after, then a mean-difference (MD) plot, each protein's
difference from the mean of the other samples against its average abundance, for the sample whose
median sat furthest from the others before normalisation.

```{r normalise-plots}
#| fig-height: 8
sample_medians <- apply(unnormalised, 2, median)
worst <- which.max(abs(sample_medians - median(sample_medians)))
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plotDensities(unnormalised, legend = FALSE, main = "Before cyclic loess")
plotDensities(proteins$E, legend = FALSE, main = "After cyclic loess")
plotMD(unnormalised, column = worst, main = paste(colnames(unnormalised)[worst], "before"))
plotMD(proteins$E, column = worst, main = paste(colnames(proteins$E)[worst], "after"))
```

Only `proteins$E` changes. Cyclic loess subtracts an abundance-dependent offset from each value
without rescaling it, so the standard errors still apply; the fitted offset is treated as known.

## Check protein estimates

Per protein: precursor count (`NPrec`, which `dpcQuant()` writes although its help page says
`NPeptides`), proportion observed, mean log2 abundance, mean standard error and mean observed
precursors per sample.

```{r quality}
protein_quality <- tibble(
  protein = rownames(proteins),
  gene = proteins$genes$Genes,
  n_precursors = proteins$genes$NPrec,
  prop_observed = proteins$genes$PropObs,
  mean_log2 = rowMeans(proteins$E),
  mean_standard_error = rowMeans(proteins$other$standard.error),
  mean_n_observations = rowMeans(proteins$other$n.observations)
)
summary(protein_quality[c("mean_log2", "mean_standard_error", "prop_observed")])
```

`plotMDSUsingSEs()` places samples by their protein profiles, weighting by the standard errors;
each point is labelled with its participant. A sample far from its own participant's other samples
is worth a look. Then the share of the first coordinate that participant and group each explain.

```{r mds}
mds <- plotMDSUsingSEs(proteins, labels = proteins$targets$participant, cex = 0.6)
round(sapply(proteins$targets[c("participant", "group")], function(f) {
  summary(lm(mds$x ~ factor(f)))$r.squared
}), 3)
```

## Slope sensitivity

The sensitivity run quantifies against the whole fitted curve, where the primary run passes
`dpc.slope = 0.7` and lets limpa fit the intercept. Both get the same detection filter, which reads
only observation counts and so keeps the same proteins, and the same normalisation. The table
gives each run's curve and mean standard error; the median absolute abundance difference follows.
It measures how far values move; `02_Differential` compares the contrasts.

```{r slope-sensitivity}
#| eval: !expr file.exists(sensitivity_file)
sensitivity <- readRDS(sensitivity_file)
sensitivity <- sensitivity[filterByDetection(sensitivity, n.samples = min(group_sizes)), ]
sensitivity$E <- normalizeBetweenArrays(sensitivity$E, method = "cyclicloess")
stopifnot(identical(rownames(sensitivity), rownames(proteins)))

tibble(
  role = c("primary", "sensitivity"),
  intercept = round(c(proteins$dpc[1], sensitivity$dpc[1]), 3),
  slope = round(c(proteins$dpc[2], sensitivity$dpc[2]), 3),
  mean_standard_error = round(c(
    mean(proteins$other$standard.error), mean(sensitivity$other$standard.error)
  ), 3)
)

round(median(abs(proteins$E - sensitivity$E)), 4)
```

The section runs only when `c_data/quant_runs/proteins_slope_fitted.rds` exists. It takes a
separate quantification run:

```sh
Rscript 01_Preprocess/02_Quantification/a_script/02_quantify_run.R --sensitivity
```

## Save results

`proteins.rds` keeps abundance, standard errors, annotations and sample metadata together for every
later stage. `02_quantify.xlsx` holds the samples, the diagnostic curve fit, detection counts and
per-protein quality.

```{r write}
sheets <- list(
  samples = as.data.frame(proteins$targets),
  dpc_parameters = dpc_parameters,
  detection_summary = data.frame(
    before = length(detected), kept = sum(detected), dropped = sum(!detected),
    minimum_samples = min(group_sizes)
  ),
  protein_quality = protein_quality
)

out <- here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data")
saveRDS(proteins, file.path(out, "proteins.rds"))
write_xlsx(sheets, file.path(out, "02_quantify.xlsx"))
```
